<Section title="Question">
<RichText>
When should a local-first developer tool prefer append-only event records over in-place mutable state, and which failure modes require snapshots or compaction?
</RichText>
</Section>

<Section title="Final answer">
Prefer append-only records when the tool must preserve authoritative transitions for audit, crash recovery, deterministic replay, offline/concurrent merge, or explain/undo workflows (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). The underlying requirement for sync is durable, mergeable causal information—not necessarily a literal event stream; CRDT state, revisioned records, or another structure can provide it (gpt-5.6-luna).

Use mutable state for ephemeral, single-writer data and replaceable projections, caches, and indexes whose history has no product value (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Keep authority separate from projections: mutable read models are safe only when they can be rebuilt or are explicitly disposable.

Add snapshots when replay or loading the authoritative history breaches the product's measured recovery/startup budget, or when memory/storage pressure makes full replay unsafe (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). A snapshot must atomically identify the exact event position it contains; recovery replays only the durable tail after that checkpoint. Keep the source log when audit or recovery requires it.

Compact only with an explicit retention policy and a safe coordination boundary. Plan and confirm the exact reclaim set; protect events needed by lagging replicas, readers, audit, replies, or forensics. Tombstone growth and storage pressure are signals, not automatic permission to delete history. A checkpoint/epoch, acknowledged retention horizon, atomic old-or-new publication, and rollback/recovery path are required (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).

There is no portable event-count or latency threshold: measure cold-start replay, peak memory, log growth, and global versus per-entity contention on the real workload (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Partitioning by entity can bound recovery work; a hot global log can create contention even when individual histories are small (gpt-5.6-luna).
</Section>

<Section title="Knowledge map">
<Tabs>
<Tab label="Shared core">
Both extraction participants support append-only authority for history, recovery, audit, and mergeable changes, while mutable state fits transient or derived data (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Both support snapshot-plus-tail and workload measurement rather than universal thresholds (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).
</Tab>
<Tab label="Unique finds">
- gpt-5.6-luna: distinguish snapshots from compaction; preserve a durable, unambiguous tail boundary; protect structured authoritative records and treat comments as an explicit schema exception.
- claude-haiku-4-5-20251001: offline sync needs causal metadata; per-entity streams can differ from a global log; storage, retention, and privacy policy determine whether compaction is acceptable.
</Tab>
<Tab label="Contradictions">
The initial claim that offline sync requires append-only events was narrowed by gpt-5.6-luna: sync requires durable causal information, not a literal event log. Numeric replay thresholds proposed by claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 were rejected as portable rules by gpt-5.6-luna. “Compaction required” for tombstones was narrowed to a retention- and coordination-dependent decision by both reviews (gpt-5.6-luna; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).
</Tab>
